The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

stakes: The Canadiens go in tied for second in the Atlantic with 16 points, the Stars tied for third in the Central with 15 points.

DAL.head: The matchup suits the Stars
DAL.body: Dallas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

MTL.head: A tough matchup for the Canadiens
MTL.body: Dallas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Clash of the titans
paras: The Stars are 7-4-1. The Canadiens have won three straight. Two of the league’s best teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Canadiens are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Stars are one of the best at keeping shots away. The Stars’ power play has a soft target in the Habs’ kill.

items.text: Chris Kreider has a point in six straight games against Dallas.
The Canadiens have been without Nick Suzuki, Samuel Montembeault and Ivan Demidov for several games. Jakub Dobeš is expected to start.
The Stars have been without Esa Lindell since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Matt Duchene all season.
Sam Steel has missed the Stars’ last two games.
